mechanisms.name: iRoPE - interleaved RoPE and NoPE layers
mechanisms.problem: Every positional scheme is a compromise between local precision and long-range reach, and picking one forces the same compromise on all 48 layers of your model. But layers are not interchangeable - some are doing local syntax and some are doing document-scale integration. Why should they share a positional scheme?
how: Do not choose. In Llama 4, roughly three layers in four use RoPE with chunked local attention (8k-token chunks) - cheap, precise, local. Every fourth layer uses no positional encoding at all with full global causal attention - unconstrained reach, and nothing that can go out of distribution at length.

The NoPE layers apply inference-time temperature scaling to the softmax, countering the entropy drift that flattens attention at extreme length - the same failure mode YaRN's temperature term addresses.
The combination is what Meta calls the iRoPE architecture, and it is what supports the claimed 10M-token context in Llama 4 Scout.
mechanisms.math: layer % 4 == 0 → NoPE + full attention;  else → RoPE + 8k chunked attention
pros: Treats the positional scheme as a per-layer choice, which in hindsight is obviously right and which nobody had shipped at scale before.
The NoPE layers have nothing to extrapolate, so the hardest length-generalisation failure is structurally absent from a quarter of the model.
Most layers stay cheap and local, so the compute profile is close to a windowed model while global reach is preserved.

It is the clearest confirmation of the timeline's positional trend: eight years of deleting positional information, ending with a frontier model that removes it from a quarter of its layers on purpose.
cons: The 10M context number is nominal, and widely disputed in practice. Independent long-context evaluations of Llama 4 were notably weaker than the headline, and effective context is far below the advertised figure. This is the clearest example on the page of a context claim that should not be taken at face value.
The 1-in-4 ratio and the 8k chunk size are unexplained empirical choices with no published ablation.
Temperature scaling at inference is a patch on a symptom rather than a principled fix.
There is no accompanying technical paper - the primary sources are a blog post and a model card, so the architecture is documented but not properly evaluated in public.
Complicates the serving stack: two different attention types with different KV behaviour in one model.
mechanisms.pick: As a design pattern if you are training a long-context model - interleaving positional and non-positional layers is a cheap idea with a clear rationale.
mechanisms.avoid: Do not use Llama 4's advertised context length as evidence that the pattern delivers 10M tokens of usable reach. Measure it yourself.
mechanisms.shipped: Llama 4 Scout and Maverick

mechanisms.name: DeepSeek sparse attention (DSA)
mechanisms.problem: NSA proved trainable sparse attention could match dense quality, but only when pretrained with it from scratch - which no one could afford to redo at frontier scale. The remaining question was whether sparsity could be introduced into an existing frontier model by continued training, and whether the economics would actually show up on a price list.
how: Add a lightning indexer: a small, cheap scoring module that computes a relevance score from each query to every preceding key. It is deliberately low-cost - few heads, low precision - because it must run over the whole history.
For each query, select the top-k keys by indexer score (k ≈ 2048, far smaller than the context) and run full MLA attention over only those. Complexity moves from O(L²) towards O(L·k).

It is introduced by continued training from DeepSeek-V3.1-Terminus rather than a fresh pretrain: first a dense warm-up phase that teaches the indexer to imitate the real attention distribution, then a sparse phase. This is the part NSA could not offer.
The commercial result is the clearest evidence on this page that the mechanism worked: API prices were cut by more than 50% on release day, with benchmark parity against the dense predecessor.
mechanisms.math: score = indexer(q, kⱼ);  attend over top-2048 keys only;  O(L·k) not O(L²)
pros: Sparse attention finally shipped in a frontier production model, at benchmark parity with its dense predecessor - the endpoint of a six-year argument.
Retrofittable by continued training, which removes the single biggest barrier to adopting NSA-style sparsity.
The price cut is externally verifiable evidence, which is rarer and more convincing than a benchmark table.
Weights and a technical report were released openly, so the claim is inspectable.
cons: The indexer still scores every previous token, so there is an irreducible linear-in-context cost before you get to save anything. The saving is on the expensive attention, not on the scan.
Top-k selection is a fixed budget of 2048 regardless of whether the query needs 5 tokens or 50,000 - a hard cap that cannot adapt to a genuinely diffuse query.
It is an experimental release by DeepSeek's own labelling, and long-horizon behaviour is not yet well characterised.
The indexer is trained to imitate the dense attention distribution, so it inherits that distribution's blind spots rather than correcting them.
Deeply co-designed with MLA and with DeepSeek's serving stack; the recipe is not obviously portable.
mechanisms.pick: The reference design if you are adding sparsity to an existing large model - the cheap-indexer-plus-top-k-plus-continued-training recipe is the transferable part.
mechanisms.avoid: Assume nothing about tasks needing more than k tokens of genuine attention breadth; the budget is fixed and the failure will be silent.
mechanisms.shipped: DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp (and the subsequent V3.2 line)

mechanisms.name: DroPE - dropping positional embeddings after pretraining
mechanisms.problem: Two facts had been sitting next to each other for years without anyone joining them. RoPE clearly helps a model converge - it is a useful inductive bias during pretraining. And RoPE is also the specific thing that breaks at long context, because the model over-relies on explicit positional signal that goes out of distribution past the training window. What if the thing that helps you train is the same thing stopping you from generalising?
how: Train normally, with RoPE, and get the convergence benefit. Then remove the positional embeddings from the trained model and run a short recalibration phase - at the original training context length, not at the target length.

The recalibrated model relies on the causal mask for positional information, exactly as a NoPE model does - but it arrived there with the benefit of having been trained with an explicit positional prior.

Because there is no positional encoding left, there is nothing to go out of distribution. The model generalises zero-shot to sequences far longer than its training window, with no long-context finetuning at all - and reportedly beats RoPE-scaling methods including NTK and YaRN on retrieval and QA.
Position ends up as scaffolding: necessary to construct the building, removed once it stands.
mechanisms.math: pretrain with RoPE  →  drop RoPE  →  short recalibration at original length  →  zero-shot long context
pros: Removes the need for long-context finetuning entirely, which is the expensive part of every method in the context-extension family above it.
Elegantly resolves a genuine tension: keep the inductive bias where it helps (training) and delete it where it hurts (extrapolation).
Nothing left to go out of distribution - it attacks the root cause rather than remapping positions around the symptom, which is what PI, NTK and YaRN all do.
It closes the eight-year positional arc on this timeline in the least obvious available direction, and it is genuinely a prediction the timeline's shape would have supported.
cons: Very new. December 2025, one lab, no independent replication, no production deployment. Treat the numbers as claims, not as settled results.
It requires access to the pretrained model and a recalibration budget - it is not a config change you can apply to an API model.
It inherits NoPE's structural constraint: it only works for causal decoders, because the causal mask is doing the positional work.
Removing a strong inductive bias after training risks capability loss in ways a short recalibration may not surface on standard benchmarks - the failure modes here are not yet mapped.

"Generalises to much longer sequences" needs the same scepticism as every other long-context claim on this page: nominal reach and effective reach are different numbers, and only one of them is easy to report.
mechanisms.pick: If you own a pretrained model and want long context without a long-context training run, this is the most interesting thing to try right now - with the caveat that you should evaluate it yourself rather than trusting the headline.
mechanisms.avoid: Anything where you cannot retrain at all, encoder models, or production use before independent replication exists.
mechanisms.shipped: Not yet - research release with an accompanying blog post
